records.text: Bayer is the only U.S. company manufacturing a form of elemental phosphorus used in glyphosate and white-phosphorus munitions.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This is from The Washington Post, because people went, why do this? They wrote: but the largely overshadowed part was the order's mention of something contentious in another way, the manufacture of munitions used by the United States military. Bayer, ... which makes glyphosate, is also the only company in the United States that manufactures a form of elemental phosphorus, which is called white phosphorus, which is used to make the weed killer. ... Phosphorus. That white phosphorus is also used to make munitions deployed as smoke screens and incendiary devices that can violently burn property or people.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 39:59. Official and company sources identify a single domestic producer of elemental phosphorus/glyphosate inputs, Bayer's U.S. operation. Elemental/white phosphorus is used in glyphosate production and has military applications, though the statement compresses chemistry and corporate structure.

sources.title: Fact Sheet: Ensuring an Adequate Supply of Elemental Phosphorus and Glyphosate-Based Herbicides - White House
sources.relevance: Confirms Bayer is the sole domestic producer of elemental phosphorus used for glyphosate and identifies national-defense uses.

records.text: Evan Hill reported that a Secret Service officer fired four times at Cole Tomas Allen and that reviewed surveillance footage showed no indication Allen fired his weapon
records.speaker: Evan Hill

appearances.snippet: Evan Hill, who is an investigative reporter for The Washington Post, wrote on his X that a Secret Service officer fired four times at Nicole Allen and in the direction of other security personnel. ... a post review of surveillance footage has been found has found that there was no indication on the foot. ... on the footage that Allen fired his weapon.

verification.notes: The Washington Post investigation states that surveillance footage showed a Secret Service officer firing four times at Cole Tomas Allen, with three shots in the general direction of other security personnel, and that the reviewed footage showed no indication Allen fired his weapon. The report also carefully notes that the footage did not capture every shot authorities alleged.

sources.title: Video shows moment Secret Service officer fired at correspondents dinner suspect
sources.relevance: Directly reports four officer shots and no indication in the reviewed footage that Allen fired.

records.text: The Washington Post reported that a 1978 congressional investigation concluded the Unification Church and Moon's other religious and secular organizations formed one international organization that moved money freely among its entities.
records.speaker: The Washington Post

appearances.snippet: In 1978, a congressional investigation into the Moon organization concluded that, quote, the unification church. And numerous other religious and secular organizations headed by Sun Myung Moon constitute essentially one international organization that moved money freely among its entities.

verification.notes: The Washington Post article directly reports that a 1978 congressional investigation concluded the Unification Church and other Moon-led religious and secular organizations constituted essentially one international organization that moved money freely among its entities. The cited congressional investigation is independently cataloged by the U.S. Government Publishing Office as the 1978 House report on Korean-American relations.
